summary: The note describes the Maxwell Land Grant, also called the Beaubien-Miranda Land Grant, a Mexican land grant from 1841 covering parts of Colfax County, New Mexico and adjoining Las Animas County, Colorado. It was one of the largest contiguous private landholdings in United States history. Several New Mexico towns, along with various ghost towns, came to be located within the grant.
one_line: The Maxwell Land Grant was an 1841 Mexican land grant in northeastern New Mexico and southern Colorado, among the largest private landholdings in US history.
key_facts: The Maxwell Land Grant was also known as the Beaubien-Miranda Land Grant.
The Maxwell Land Grant was a Mexican land grant.
The Maxwell Land Grant was made in 1841.
The Maxwell Land Grant was located in Colfax County, New Mexico.
The Maxwell Land Grant included part of Las Animas County, Colorado.
The Maxwell Land Grant was one of the largest contiguous private landholdings in the history of the United States.
The New Mexico towns of Cimarron, Colfax, Dawson, Elizabethtown, French, Lynn, Maxwell, Miami, Raton, Rayado, Springer, Ute Park and Vermejo Park came to be located within the Maxwell Land Grant.
Numerous other towns that are now ghost towns were also located within the Maxwell Land Grant.
